reconstruction.reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner product space carrying its normed additive commutative group structure and its Borel measurable structure. Let V:E->R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable, alpha,beta be nonnegative real parameters, and eta be real. Assume 0<alpha, alpha<=beta, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. For every x,v:E assume both
  alpha*||v||^2 <= (D(DV)(x)[v])[v],
  (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] <= beta*||v||^2.
Use real coercions of alpha,beta in these formulas. DV(x) is a bounded real-linear functional on E, and D(DV)(x)[v] is another such functional. These data, structures and inequalities exhaust the caller premises.

Define mu as the normalized exponential tilt of volume on E by x->-V(x). Define J as the pushforward of mu times stdGaussian(E) by (x,z)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*z). Set nu=J.snd. Define Lambda as the pushforward of J by (x,y)->(y,2*x-y), and F(x,y)=(x,2*x-y). Thus J uses coordinates (x,y), whereas Lambda uses coordinates (y,2*x-y).

Use the product measurable structure on E x E. Set mY=comap(second-coordinate map, the measurable structure of E); the inclusion of mY in the product sigma algebra is derived internally from measurability of that projection. Let H=L2(J) and K=L2(nu), complete real Hilbert spaces of square-integrable measurable almost-everywhere classes. Let HP=lpMeas(R,R,mY,2,J), the closed mY-measurable subspace of H, with inclusion i:HP->H and orthogonal projection pi:H->HP. Define P:H->H by inclusion composed with L2 conditional expectation onto mY. Let M:K->H be the real-linear isometric pullback by the second-coordinate map; its measure-preserving witness is derived internally from nu=J.snd.

The measures mu,J,nu are probability measures. HP is exactly the algebraic range of P.toLinearMap, and P(i(f))=i(f) for every f:HP.

There exists a Markov kernel S from E to E such that for every y:E, as an exact equality of measures,
  S(y)=volume.tilted(x->-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8*eta)).
This normalized formula is every-state. S is a conditional kernel of Lambda, with the second coordinate conditioned on the first in the supplied IsCondKernel sense. Lambda.fst=nu and Lambda.snd=nu.

There exists a real-linear isometric equivalence e:K->HP onto that exact subspace, with i(e(u))=M(u) for every u:K. There exists a real-linear isometry U:H->H such that, separately for every g:H, the representative of U(g) equals g composed with F J-almost everywhere. U is involutive, U(U(g))=g for every g, and U.toContinuousLinearMap is selfadjoint.

There exists a bounded real-linear endomorphism T:K->K which is selfadjoint and satisfies, for every u:K, all three statements:
  ||T(u)||<=||u||,
  T(u)(y)=integral u(x) dS(y)(x) for nu-almost every y,
  integral T(u)(y) dnu(y)=integral u(y) dnu(y).
The representative formulas for U and T are per-observable AE formulas; they do not assert a common exceptional set for all observables.

Define A:HP->HP by A=pi composed with U composed with i, and B:HP->H by B=(I_H-P) composed with U composed with P composed with i. Then A=e composed with T composed with e^{-1}; A is selfadjoint; ||A(f)||<=||f|| for every f:HP; and P(B(f))=0 for every f:HP.

There exists a positive bounded endomorphism Gamma:K->K satisfying Gamma composed with Gamma=I_K-T composed with T. Define GammaP:HP->HP by GammaP=e composed with Gamma composed with e^{-1}. Then GammaP is positive, GammaP composed with GammaP=I_HP-A composed with A, and
  B.adjoint composed with B=GammaP composed with GammaP.
Here B.adjoint:H->HP. Gamma,GammaP are operator square roots, not real numbers. Positivity includes selfadjointness and a nonnegative real quadratic form.

There exists q:K with representative equal to 1 nu-almost everywhere, T(q)=q, and <q,u>_K=integral u(y) dnu(y) for every u:K. Set qP=e(q), and define HP0 exactly as ker(innerSL R qP) inside HP: the kernel of the continuous real-linear functional f-><qP,f>_HP. HP0 has the inherited normed additive group and real inner product, and its completeness is obtained internally from closedness of this kernel. Define
  gamma=2*sqrt(alpha*eta)/(1+alpha*eta).
For every f:HP, f belongs to HP0 if and only if integral (e^{-1}(f))(y) dnu(y)=0. Also GammaP(qP)=0 and gamma>0.

There exists a bounded real-linear endomorphism GammaP0:HP0->HP0 which, after inclusion into HP, equals GammaP applied to the inclusion of f for every f:HP0. It is positive; GammaP0-gamma*I_HP0 is positive; and it is a unit in the algebra of bounded endomorphisms of HP0. There exists a bounded endomorphism Inv:HP0->HP0 with both
  Inv composed with GammaP0=I_HP0,
  GammaP0 composed with Inv=I_HP0,
and operator-norm bound ||Inv||<=1/gamma.

Define Hperp exactly as ker(P) inside H, and equip it with its inherited normed additive group and real inner product and the completeness derived internally from closedness of P's kernel. This is the space of L2(J) classes with zero conditional expectation onto mY, not a replacement by the globally zero-mean classes.

There exists B0:HP0->Hperp, a bounded real-linear map, such that for every f:HP0 its inclusion into H equals B applied to the inclusion of f into HP. There exists a bounded real-linear map V0:HP0->Hperp satisfying
  V0=B0 composed with Inv,
  B0=V0 composed with GammaP0,
  V0.adjoint composed with V0=I_HP0,
and, for every f:HP0, ||V0(f)||=||f|| with the inherited norms. Here V0.adjoint has domain Hperp and codomain HP0. The adjoint identity is an identity on HP0. It asserts a linear isometric embedding into Hperp and a domain-side left inverse, not onto-ness, not V0 composed with V0.adjoint=I_Hperp, and not a two-sided inverse between these subspaces.

All caller data and structures are universal subject to the original hypotheses. The produced witnesses, in their dependent order, are S,e,U,T,Gamma,q,GammaP0,Inv,B0,V0. All measures, projections, pullback witnesses, conjugates, constants, subspaces and inherited Hilbert instances are definitions or internal constructions, not extra public premises. No inverse of the full operator GammaP on HP is asserted: GammaP(qP)=0 is explicit. No nontriviality or positive dimension is assumed for E, HP0 or Hperp; their zero-space cases retain their own identity-operator meaning. The every-vector norm equality for V0 remains valid on a zero domain and does not assert its operator norm is 1 in that case. alpha=0 and eta=0 are excluded. All measure, range, vector, operator and inverse identities are exact at their stated types; the specifically marked representative formulas are AE.
scopes: Normalized tilts and all operator/measure identities use their displayed domains. Endomorphism products mean composition. Gamma roots are operators, while gamma,sqrt(eta) are real scalars.
Every-state normalized kernel formula is distinct from conditional actions, which are AE per observable and need not share a null set. Disintegration stays in the supplied IsCondKernel sense.
HP0 is a globally centered subspace of HP via e^{-1}. Hperp is zero conditional expectation in H: requiring Pg=0 is stronger than only zero total integral and cannot be replaced by global centering.
V0.adjoint V0=I_HP0 is a domain-side isometry identity, not an onto/reverse-product identity. It does not assert V0 V0.adjoint=I_Hperp, a unitary equivalence or a two-sided inverse for V0.

Closed-kernel Hilbert structures and all witnesses are produced internally. The inverse Inv acts only on HP0. Zero-dimensional/trivial spaces are allowed; alpha=0 and eta=0 are excluded; no unconditional norm(V0)=1 claim on a trivial domain.
Packet says compiled, but no compiler or source-fidelity review is performed.
